content.value_statement: Value-based bidding can optimize toward revenue that does not reflect profit. This skill creates a documented conversion value model using margins, proxy values, and reconciliation checks.
actual_capabilities: Inventories revenue and non-revenue conversion actions in scope.
Defines dynamic or static values for revenue-bearing conversions.
Applies margin or COGS inputs to calculate net conversion value.
Derives documented proxy values for leads, calls, and signups.
Checks for value-rule double adjustments and value-to-profit gaps.
Produces a launch-readiness decision and a value QA sheet.
limitations: It does not verify that conversion tags fire or that UTMs are correct.
It cannot calculate margins without user-provided margin or COGS data.
It does not reconcile cross-platform attribution or deduplicate orders.
It provides a planning specification, not direct ad-platform configuration.

use_cases.title: Prepare ecommerce profit bidding
use_cases.description: Map product or category margins onto purchase values before launching tROAS bidding.

use_cases.title: Value lead-generation actions
use_cases.description: Derive evidence-based proxy values for leads, calls, and newsletter signups.

use_cases.title: Review agency measurement plans
use_cases.description: Check whether proposed conversion values reflect booked contribution rather than raw order count.

prompt_templates.title: Start a value model
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a conversion value model for my purchase and lead conversions. My bid goal is tROAS.

prompt_templates.title: Add margin adjustments
prompt_templates.prompt: Map these category margins onto my GA4 purchase values and identify the required net-value formula.

prompt_templates.title: Set lead proxy values
prompt_templates.prompt: Derive proxy values for leads and phone calls using my close rate, average order value, and margin.

prompt_templates.title: Audit launch readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my conversion values, value rules, and recent platform totals. Identify double adjustments and decide whether value-based bidding is launch-ready.

output_examples.input: Purchase revenue is dynamic. Category A margin is 40 percent and Category B margin is 25 percent.
output: Net value: revenue multiplied by the applicable category margin.
Decision: use category-level margin inputs; do not add a rule that repeats the same adjustment.

output_examples.input: A lead closes at 20 percent. Average order value is 500 dollars. Net margin is 30 percent.
output: Derivation: 500 dollars multiplied by 30 percent margin multiplied by 20 percent close rate.
Status: label as estimated and validate against booked results.

best_practices: Use measured transaction and margin data whenever it is available.
Label each value as measured, user-provided, or estimated.
Reconcile summed platform value against booked net contribution before launch.
anti_patterns: Do not use a guessed round proxy value without a documented derivation.
Do not apply a value rule that double-adjusts an already netted value.
Do not treat a value model as proof that conversion tracking works.

faq.question: What bid goals does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports tROAS, maximum conversion value, and similar value-based bidding goals.

faq.question: Do I need margin data?
faq.answer: Margin or COGS data is needed to optimize toward profit. Without it, the skill marks the value as needing input.

faq.question: Can it value leads and phone calls?
faq.answer: Yes. It derives a proxy from expected downstream net value when close-rate and order data are available.

faq.question: Does it configure Google Ads or Meta directly?
faq.answer: No. It produces a value-model specification and QA guidance for manual implementation.

faq.question: Does it test conversion tags?
faq.answer: No. Use a conversion-signal QA process to verify event firing and UTM quality.

faq.question: Will it save my business data?
faq.answer: It asks before saving results for future sessions and does not write memory without approval.
